Change c0397. Location: 1818 Vol. III, Ch. IV; 1831 Ch. XXI.

Context before (unchanged): They instantly carried it to the cottage of an old woman near the spot, and endeavoured, but in vain, to restore it to life.

1818 text: He appeared to be a handsome young man, about five and twenty years of age.

1831 text: It appeared to be a handsome young man, about five and twenty years of age.

Diff: [-He-] {+It+} appeared to be a handsome young man, about five and twenty years of age.

Context after (unchanged): He had apparently been strangled; for there was no sign of any violence, except the black mark of fingers on his neck.

result.rationale: Pronoun swap "He" to "It" for Clerval's corpse, following the context's "it" (the body). Largely a stylistic/grammatical alignment, but it slightly depersonalizes the dead Clerval before "He had apparently been strangled" restores personhood.
